source.title: From Theory to Decision Rule: Calibrating the Noisy-Label Crossover for VLM Weak Supervision Across Three Medical-Imaging Benchmarks
source.authors: Bruce Changlong Xu; Jose K. James; Alexander J. Ryu

page_placements.theme: A weaker teacher used alongside ground-truth labels (reverse or weak-teacher distillation, weak feedback to an already supervised model)

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests weak-label training and crossover behavior on medical-imaging vision tasks, extending the finding to VLM labelers and compact image-classification students rather than reproducing the original language-model setup.
record.gate_note: The paper reports gold-only versus gold-plus-weak AUC grids, architecture and modality comparisons, structured-versus-random label comparisons, loss variants, and toxic-class results. It does not calculate Burns et al.'s PGR. Its student training mixes expert gold labels with weak labels; the rows therefore report AUC and comparisons with stated VLM ceilings, not PGR. The paper's theoretical derivations are not empirical result rows.
record.test_reason: A frozen VLM labeler (BiomedCLIP, about 0.84/0.615/0.620 AUC) trains compact CNN students that reach about 0.97 AUC on gold labels, so the students are more capable than their labeler. The near-weak-only cells (ng ≤ 20–100 with 5K–50K weak labels) and the six-architecture weak-ceiling sweep show whether the student beats its weak supervisor in vision. Two caveats: students always get some gold labels, and PGR is never computed. Higher-gold crossover cells measure a different construct: whether weak labels help gold-only training.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. Add the authors' central claim: the weak-dominated student ceiling equals the VLM labeler's accuracy regardless of student architecture (8M–89M). On their reading, the labeler, not student capacity, binds, and students do not surpass it without enough gold labels.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains compact image classifiers on mixtures of expert gold labels and VLM-generated weak labels and evaluates AUC crossovers; it does not use the original strong-language-model fine-tuning setup or report PGR.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with gold-label budget, dataset and label granularity, student architecture, weak-label source, prompt template, confidence filtering, and training loss. The paper reports different crossover ranges across PCAM, ISIC 2019, and NIH ChestX-ray14.

fits_no_version.finding: Gold-vs-weak crossover: weak labels raise AUC over gold-only training only while gold-only AUC is below the labeler's ceiling (PCAM ng≈100, ISIC 20–50, NIH 250–500), and lower it above that point.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Adding a weaker labeler's pseudo-labels to gold training helps only below the gold budget where gold-only performance matches the labeler.

fits_no_version.finding: Above the crossover, GCE and Co-teaching recover +0.06 to +0.13 AUC over hard-label merging but stay below gold-only training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise-robust losses soften, but do not remove, harm from weak labels in gold-dominated training.

record.peer_reviewed: Accepted at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Combining Theory and Benchmarks (CTB); extended preprint.
record.problems: PGR is not computed, and the principal comparisons use mixtures of gold and weak labels rather than weak labels alone. Several reported weak-augmented grid values have no uncertainty shown. The study reports in-distribution benchmark splits and notes that cross-hospital distribution shift is future work. The decision-rule audit includes small validation budgets and has seed-level disagreement at tiny ISIC budgets.
record.rows_left_out: Table 1 and Table 2 also report weak-label doses other than the selected PCAM 50K, ISIC 5K, and NIH 5K crossover series; those dose-by-budget cells are omitted to stay within the row limit. Table 4 includes no additional gold budgets beyond the selected structured-versus-random comparisons recorded here. Table 5 reports per-pathology ceilings, crossovers, and effects for all 15 NIH labels; only the No Finding weak-supervision result is retained. The separate prompt-sensitivity and PubMedCLIP grids, confidence-filtering results, decision-rule audit, and most class-level results are not extracted as rows.

untested.parts: Pure weak-label training with no gold labels; PGR is never computed.
Auxiliary confidence loss and ensembling weak supervisors. Bootstrapping is not tested.
Supervisor size scaling (one labeler size each), NLP, chess and reward modelling tasks, and representation-level predictors.
Student exploiting what the supervisor can't check; distribution shift (named as future work); measured weak–strong error agreement.
No empirical test. Theorem 3.3(iii) argues the student converges to the labeler's ceiling under systematic errors, a counter-condition stated only theoretically.

missing.what: Low-gold loss sweep (ng = 10–100), the regime that bears on V2: all losses cluster near or below hard-label BCE and below the labeler AUC.
PubMedCLIP labeler on ISIC: weak-dominated student 0.556 equals labeler ceiling 0.556 at ng = 10 (no gain over supervisor).
ResNet-50 (25M) vs DenseNet-121 on ISIC: weak-dominated values 0.593–0.612, no gain with student size.
Per-class labeler ceiling vs weak-supervision gain across all 15 NIH classes (monotone with labeler AUC).
Prompt sweep: labeler ceiling 0.539–0.671 changes the student outcome in step.

record.verdict_notes: Framed as noisy-label/VLM pseudo-labelling, not weak-to-strong. The supervisor (400M VLM) is larger than the students, but less accurate on the task than gold-trained students (0.97 vs 0.84 on PCAM). Every condition mixes in some gold labels, so even the weak-dominated cells are not pure weak-to-strong. The record's V1/V6 'supports' labels came from high-gold cells where gold-only already beats the labeler; those are reassigned to fits_no_version. Burns et al.'s own vision experiments found positive PGR; this study finds about zero in medical imaging. Possible reasons are compact CNN students, coarse binary prompts tiled across classes, and systematic labeler errors. Internal inconsistencies: ISIC grid subject (DenseNet-121 vs ResNet-18), and the Table 11 hard-label value (0.597) vs Table 2 (0.672) at ng = 500.

versions.untested_parts: PGR itself is not calculated. Students are trained on mixtures of gold and weak labels, not solely on weak labels; results are AUC comparisons with the stated VLM ceiling.
The reported training-objective sweep tests confidence-weighted BCE, soft-label distillation, GCE, and Co-teaching; it does not test auxiliary confidence loss or ensembling weak supervisors.
The study varies student architectures, imaging tasks, labelers, prompts, training budgets, and pathology classes. It does not test representation-level predictors of PGR as defined in the claim.
The study compares structured VLM noise with rate-matched random noise and reports toxic classes. It does not test distribution shift or whether weak and strong models' shared errors reduce PGR.
The paper derives a noisy-label crossover model, but does not test conditions under which a strong student must beat its weak supervisor.
Tests medical-imaging vision tasks; does not test other non-language modalities beyond vision.
